en.name: Buckwheat flour
en.summary: Buckwheat flour keeps just 1 month in the pantry and 2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F) — the shortest window of any flour on this site. Buckwheat is milled whole, it is high in unsaturated oil, and that oil turns rancid fast.
en.pantry: 1 month in an airtight container somewhere cool, dark and dry, and treat that as a real limit rather than a cautious one. Buckwheat is not a cereal at all but a seed, and it is milled with the germ in, so the flour carries a high proportion of unsaturated oil — the kind that oxidises fastest. Anyone who has made soba knows the smell of fresh buckwheat flour: green, nutty and faintly floral. A month-old bag in a warm kitchen smells sharp and bitter instead, and that bitterness carries straight into the noodles or the galettes. Darker flour, milled with more of the hull, goes first.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for buckwheat flour. Cold storage genuinely helps here more than for most flours, because oxidation is the whole problem, but an airtight container is not optional: buckwheat flour takes up moisture and fridge odours readily, and a cold bag opened in a warm kitchen condenses water straight into it. Given the choice, put it in the freezer rather than the fridge.
en.freezer: 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F), which is short for a freezer figure and tells you how reactive this flour is. Double-bag or use an airtight tub with the air pressed out, and label it. Kept continuously frozen the flour stays safe well past that; what runs out is the flavour that made you buy buckwheat in the first place. Let the sealed container come back to room temperature before opening so the flour does not pick up condensation.
en.thawing: Bring the sealed container up to room temperature before opening it. Small quantities can go straight from frozen into a batter without trouble.
spoilage: A sharp, bitter or paint-like smell instead of a green, nutty one.
Bitterness in the finished noodles or pancakes, which is the clearest test.
Colour gone dull grey-brown and flat.
Clumping, webbing or larvae in the bag, all of which mean it goes out.
tips: Buy small bags and buy them often; this is not a flour to stockpile.
Smell the bag every time — buckwheat tells you honestly when it has gone.
Darker, hull-rich flour is more flavourful and spoils faster; plan accordingly.
Freeze whole buckwheat groats instead and grind as needed if you use it rarely.

faq.q: How long does buckwheat flour last?
faq.a: 1 month in an airtight container in the pantry, or 2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why does buckwheat flour go off so fast?
faq.a: It is a whole-seed flour high in unsaturated oil, and unsaturated oil oxidises quickly. Rancidity, not spoilage organisms, is what ends a bag.

faq.q: How can you tell if buckwheat flour is still good?
faq.a: Smell it. Fresh buckwheat is green, nutty and faintly floral; stale buckwheat is sharp and bitter, and that bitterness comes through in the food.

zh.name: 蕎麥粉
zh.summary: 蕎麥粉密封放常溫只能放 1 個月，−18 °C 冷凍是 2 個月——這是本站所有麵粉裡最短的。蕎麥是整粒磨的，不飽和油脂比例高，而那種油耗得特別快。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐、放陰涼避光乾燥處，1 個月；請把這當成真正的上限，不是保守的說法。蕎麥根本不是穀類而是一種種子，而且連胚芽一起磨，所以粉裡帶著高比例的不飽和油脂——也就是最容易氧化的那一種。做過蕎麥麵的人都認得新鮮蕎麥粉的氣味：帶青草感、堅果香，還有一點花香。同一包放在溫暖廚房裡一個月後，聞起來會變得刺鼻發苦，而那股苦味會原封不動地跑進麵條或可麗餅裡。帶殼比例高、顏色較深的粉壞得更快。
zh.fridge: 蕎麥粉沒有公布的冷藏期限。低溫對它的幫助確實比對多數麵粉都大，因為氧化就是它唯一的問題；但密封容器不是可選項：蕎麥粉很會吸濕也很會吸冰箱的味道，一包冰過的粉在溫暖廚房裡打開，水氣會直接凝進粉裡。如果要選，請放冷凍而不是冷藏。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 2 個月。以冷凍數字來說這很短，也說明了這種粉有多活潑。套兩層袋或用密封罐、壓出空氣，並貼上標籤。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；先用完的是「你當初為什麼要買蕎麥」的那個風味。開蓋前先讓整罐回到室溫，粉才不會受潮。
zh.thawing: 整罐密封著回到室溫再開蓋。少量的話，直接從冷凍加進麵糊裡也沒問題。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、發苦或帶油漆味，而不是青草堅果香。
做出來的麵條或煎餅發苦，這是最準的測試。
顏色變成暗沉的灰褐色、毫無生氣。
結塊、出現絲網或幼蟲——這些都表示整袋該丟。
tips: 少量勤買；這不是可以囤的粉。
每次都聞一下——蕎麥壞了會誠實告訴你。
顏色深、帶殼多的粉風味更好也壞得更快，請據此安排。
如果很少用，改成冷凍蕎麥粒、要用再磨。

faq.a: 密封放常溫 1 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 2 個月。

faq.q: 蕎麥粉為什麼壞得這麼快？
faq.a: 它是整粒磨的、不飽和油脂比例高，而不飽和油脂氧化得很快。結束一包蕎麥粉的是油耗，不是腐敗菌。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷蕎麥粉還能不能用？
faq.a: 聞一下。新鮮的帶青草、堅果與一點花香；走味的刺鼻發苦，而那股苦會跑進食物裡。
